findings.rationale: Sex=1 subgroup at SC: observed outcome rate 0.014 vs mean predicted risk 0.128 (O/E 0.11, z_noise about -12), i.e. positives in this subgroup are systematically recorded as negative. SC's updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 3.09, mean cos -0.26, z about -6.5 on cos and +6.4 on norm), consistent with the client training away from the federation on corrupted labels. Its overall AUC and ECE look normal, so this is a label/under-diagnosis problem rather than poisoning. Onset is not directly resolvable from the pooled subgroup screen; the fault is taken to be present from round 1, since the signature is stable across rounds.

Sex=1 subgroup at TX: observed outcome rate 0.0039 vs mean predicted risk 0.121 (O/E 0.03, FNR 0, z_noise about -13), so positives in this subgroup are recorded as negative. TX's updates are anomalous (median norm ratio 2.88, mean cos -0.20, z about -6.1 on cos and +5.9 on norm) and its pooled CITL is positive (z +3.4), consistent with missing positives. Local AUC is normal, which points to label under-recording rather than poisoning. Onset is taken as round 1 because the signature is stable across rounds.

Sex=1 subgroup at WA: observed outcome rate 0.0148 vs mean predicted risk 0.115 (O/E 0.13, z_noise about -12.8), indicating positives recorded as negative in this subgroup. WA is the largest client (n about 11k) and has the strongest update anomaly (median norm ratio 5.6, mean cos -0.10, z +6.2 on norm and -5.4 on cos). Its pooled CITL is strongly positive (z +3.9), and CITL is already +0.27 in round 1, so the bias is present from the start. Local AUC is normal, which points to subgroup label under-recording rather than poisoning.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup), then spent the remaining budget on per-round checks of SC, TX, WA and GU. Three clients (SC, TX, WA) show the same consistent signature: under-recorded positives in the Sex=1 subgroup (O/E 0.03 to 0.13, z_noise about -12 to -13), together with anomalous update norms (3 to 5.6x median) and negative cosine to the median update. Their local AUC is normal, so I classified this as subgroup_bias rather than poisoning, with onset round 1. Not reported, as too weak or unconfirmed: NC (GenHlth p99 z_noise -6.1, with a drift onset flag at round 17 but no drift flag and no mean shift), GU (high O/E in Sex=1 and small-sample CITL, with noisy per-round updates), and several drift-onset flags on small clients (DC, NV, VI, NH, SD, VA), which look like noise. Budget is now exhausted (0 remaining).
